author: ISAB’s Burner
title: Lots of potential, not fully realized
content:
TLDR: Good game with no ads or bugs, but it has a repetitive gameplay loop and feels a bit “grindy”.

Bloons Blitz is similar to any other survivor games I’ve played: clear levels to get gold and loot boxes that allow you to upgrade towers and heroes. However, after a while it seems like gold is a rare commodity, and leveling up towers becomes harder and harder if you don’t pay real money. Would I prefer the game have ads over this? Probably not, but it’s something to consider.
A second note is the repetitive gameplay and lack of content. I’m sure NinjaKiwi will add more towers and heroes soon, but right now the gameplay loop is so sparse that I had to comment on it.
Mechanically, however, the game is great. Everything is intuitive and there’s no crazy bugs that I’ve seen so far. You can definitely create some awesome builds already with the limited tower selection, and the game provides power-ups to help with that (banish, pin, reroll etc.). It’s a good game with potential to become great!

author: CommonDartMonkey
title: I wish the game would’ve just been paid
content:
I have been playing bloons games since the original flash version of Bloons TD, and I love them all a lot! It’s cool that it’s a free game to play, but the consequences of that decision are very apparent in this game. Every single menu in this game is asking you to spend money to get ahead. The core gameplay is very fun and I have a had a great time playing thus far. However, the game tries very hard to let you know that you are the product and begs you to spend money on it. 

In terms of gameplay, the upgrades are a lot of fun to play with, but as soon as you start getting good upgrades during your run, it’s already time for the final boss fight and it all ends. The game seems to be laid out like the fun is going to the next level, not what happens within each level. I hope they add an endless mode in the future or do something along the lines of Vampire Survivor allow the run to go to 30 minutes. 

I was hoping the harder modes had increased playtime and more bloons within each run. However, it seems to be called hard because they decrease the amount of “blops” you get leading to less upgrades. 

I can’t discount the game too much for having a free to play model,  because that’s just the nature of the beast. However, I hope they add something to the game that allows individual runs to last longer and not end just as they’re getting good. Additionally, more balancing is needed for the hero’s. Quincy is far and wide the best hero out at the moment. Obin’s wolf AI is very difficult to work with during boss fights and it doesn’t have enough pierce. 

Overall, the game is a lot of fun to play here and there, but its main fallbacks come from the details. I am excited for new updates to come out and to “pop” back in for possible new modes, towers, and heroes!

author: FaZe_Yomama07
title: Perfect Game
content:
Blood Blitz TD is an incredibly fun and addictive wave-defense game that does a great job of keeping you engaged from the moment you start playing. The gameplay is straightforward enough to pick up quickly, but there’s enough strategy, progression, and increasing difficulty to keep each run feeling exciting.

The wave-based gameplay is easily one of my favorite parts. Each wave feels like a new challenge, and as the enemies become stronger and more numerous, you’re constantly having to think about how you want to approach the next round. There’s a really satisfying feeling that comes from surviving a difficult wave when it looks like you’re completely overwhelmed.

The combat also feels incredibly rewarding. There’s something satisfying about clearing out a massive group of enemies and watching your character become stronger as you progress. The game does a great job of creating that “one more wave” feeling where you keep telling yourself you’ll stop after the next round, only to end up playing for another hour.

I also really enjoy the progression system. Getting stronger over time gives you a genuine sense of improvement, and it makes each run feel like it contributes toward something. You’re not just repeatedly playing the same waves—you’re building toward being able to survive longer and take on bigger challenges.

The visual style and overall atmosphere fit the game extremely well. The bloodier aesthetic gives Blood Blitz TD its own identity, and the chaos of having huge numbers of enemies coming at you makes the later waves especially satisfying.

Another major strength is the replayability. The game has the kind of gameplay loop that makes you want to keep experimenting and see how far you can get. Even when a run ends, it’s easy to immediately think, “I could have made it further if I did this differently,” which is exactly what you want from a game like this.

Obviously, there’s always room for more content as the game develops. More enemies, abilities, maps, upgrades, challenges, and different ways to approach each run could make an already enjoyable experience even deeper. But the core gameplay is already extremely solid.

Overall, Blood Blitz TD is a fast-paced, satisfying, and genuinely addictive wave-defense game. It’s easy to pick up, difficult to put down, and has a great progression loop that makes you want to keep pushing further with every run.

5/5 stars. Highly recommend it to anyone who enjoys intense wave-based survival and action games.
